day.1.character.action: Do one good deed today completely in secret, such as charity, helping someone or a quiet du'a, and tell no one.
day.1.character.description: Sincerity means doing things for the pleasure of Allah alone, not for praise or recognition.
day.1.dhikr.ainni_ala_dhikrik.meaning: (At the end of each prayer) O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You and worship You well
day.1.dhikr.alhamdulillah.meaning: (After each prayer) All praise is for Allah
day.1.dhikr.allahuakbar.meaning: (After each prayer) Allah is the Greatest
day.1.dhikr.basmalah.meaning: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
day.1.dhikr.shahadah.meaning: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah
day.1.dhikr.subhanallah.meaning: (After each prayer) Glory be to Allah
day.1.dhikr.tahlil.meaning: (The 100th, after the tasbih) None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things
day.1.hadith.meaning: "Actions are only by intentions, and each person will only have what he intended."
day.1.intro: Every act begins with intention. Today you lay the foundation of your path by purifying your heart and renewing your commitment to Allah.
day.1.prayer.dua.meaning: (After the salam of Fajr) O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision and accepted deeds.
day.1.prayer.tip: Wake up 10 minutes before Fajr. Sit quietly, make wudu with intention, and pray Fajr with your full attention. After the salam, say this du'a.
day.1.quran.note: Read Al-Fatihah slowly and reflect on each verse. You recite it in every rak'ah: "Guide us to the straight path."
day.1.reflection: What is your true intention for walking this path? Write it down and keep it as your anchor.
day.1.sunnah.description: Say "Bismillah" before you eat, drink, leave the house or start your work. The Prophet ﷺ said to a boy: "Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you."

day.1.task.1_fajr.titleAdvanced: Pray Fajr on time with its 2 sunnah rak'ahs and the du'a after the salam

day.1.task.1_reflection.title: Write down your intention for this path
day.1.task.1_secret_deed.title: Do one good deed in secret
day.10.character.action: Write a heartfelt list of 10 things you need from Allah. Be specific, then trust Him and let go.
day.10.character.description: Du'a is an expression of tawakkul: knowing that everything is in Allah's hands and that He alone can help.
day.10.dhikr.hamm_wal_hazan.meaning: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from the burden of debt and from being overpowered by men
day.10.dhikr.tahlil.meaning: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things
day.10.hadith.meaning: "Supplication is worship itself." Then he recited: "And your Lord says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you" (Ghafir 40:60).
day.10.intro: Du'a is worship itself, and Allah says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you." Today you learn to speak to Allah in your own words and trust in His answer.
day.10.prayer.dua.meaning: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
day.10.prayer.tip: In every sujood today, make du'a in your own words for your needs, your family and the ummah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so make much du'a." Anas said this Quranic du'a was the one he made most often (Bukhari 6389).
day.10.quran.note: The verse that shows Allah is always near and always listening: "I am near. I respond to the call of the one who calls upon Me."
day.10.reflection: Have you ever felt a du'a of yours was answered? What did it feel like? Are there du'as you have stopped hoping for?
day.10.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ taught us special times for du'a: the last third of the night (Bukhari 1145), between the adhan and the iqamah (Abu Dawud 521; Tirmidhi 212), in sujood (Muslim 482), at the end of the obligatory prayers (Tirmidhi 3499), and the hour on Friday, sought in the last hour after Asr (Bukhari 935; Abu Dawud 1048). Use at least 3 of these times today.

day.11.character.action: Give sadaqah today, even a small coin, a smile or some food. Give something that costs you something.
day.11.character.description: True generosity is giving when it is hard to give, giving what you love, and expecting nothing in return.
day.11.dhikr.bismillah_before_eating.mea: (Before eating) In the name of Allah
day.11.dhikr.subhanallahi_wa_bihamdihi.m: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him
day.11.dhikr.yunfiqu_fa_tukhlif.meaning: (Personal du'a, inspired by the angels' du'a in Bukhari 1442) O Allah, make us among those who spend, and You replace it for them
day.11.hadith.meaning: "Charity does not decrease wealth, and Allah does not increase a servant who forgives except in honour."
day.11.intro: Giving in the way of Allah purifies your wealth, eases hardship and earns His love. The Prophet ﷺ was the most generous of people, and even more generous in Ramadan.
day.11.prayer.tip: Every morning two angels come down. One says, "O Allah, give the one who spends something in return," and the other says, "O Allah, give the one who withholds loss" (Bukhari 1442; Muslim 1010). Give some sadaqah early today, after Fajr.
day.11.quran.note: The parable of those who spend in the way of Allah: like a grain that grows seven ears, with a hundred grains in each ear. "And Allah multiplies for whom He wills."
day.11.reflection: What are you holding back from giving: money, time, knowledge or kindness? What would happen if you gave more?
day.11.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, knowledge that benefits, or a righteous child who prays for him." Start an ongoing charity today: share beneficial knowledge, teach someone a Sunnah, plant a tree, give to a masjid fund or support an orphan.
day.11.sunnah.title: Sadaqah jariyah (ongoing charity)
day.11.task.11_dhikr.title: Say SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi 100 times
day.11.task.11_ongoing.title: Do one act of ongoing charity (sadaqah jariyah)

day.12.character.action: Practise contentment today: hold back from one purchase or desire you would normally give in to, and say "Alhamdulillah" for what you have.
day.12.character.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Wealth is not having many possessions; true wealth is contentment of the soul" (Bukhari 6446).
day.12.dhikr.astaghfirullah.meaning: I seek Allah's forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness a hundred times a day.
day.12.dhikr.audhu_minal_faqr.meaning: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from poverty, from scarcity and from humiliation, and I seek refuge in You from wronging others or being wronged
day.12.dhikr.ikfini_bi_halalik.meaning: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful instead of what You have forbidden, and by Your grace make me free of need of anyone besides You
day.12.hadith.meaning: "O people, Allah is Good and accepts only what is good."
day.12.intro: What we earn and consume shapes our hearts and our worship. Today, look at your livelihood in the light of Islam.
day.12.prayer.tip: Pray 2 rak'ahs of Duha today, between sunrise and Dhuhr. Every morning a charity is due for each joint of your body, and two rak'ahs of Duha suffice for all of it (Muslim 720).
day.12.quran.note: Allah commands us to eat of what is lawful and good, and warns us not to follow the footsteps of Shaytan: "Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy."
day.12.reflection: Is there anything in how you earn or spend money that you need to review in the light of Islam?
day.12.sunnah.description: Make this du'a often: "Allahummak-fini bi-halalika 'an haramika wa aghnini bi-fadlika 'amman siwak" (O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful instead of what You have forbidden, and make me free of need of anyone besides You). After Fajr, also ask Allah for "beneficial knowledge, good provision and accepted deeds" (Ibn Majah 925).

day.13.character.action: Write down your top 3 worries. Then sincerely hand each one to Allah's care, saying "Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil."
day.13.character.description: Much anxiety comes from trying to control outcomes. Tawakkul replaces anxiety with peace, because Allah is in control.
day.13.dhikr.hasbunallah.meaning: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs
day.13.dhikr.leaving_home_dua.meaning: (On leaving home) In the name of Allah; I place my trust in Allah; there is no might nor power except by Allah
day.13.dhikr.tahlil.meaning: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things
day.13.hadith.meaning: "If you relied on Allah as He truly deserves, you would be provided for as the birds are provided for: they go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening."
day.13.intro: Tawakkul means doing your best and then placing the result entirely in Allah's hands. It is not laziness; it is one of the highest levels of faith.
day.13.prayer.tip: If you have a decision to make, big or small, pray istikhara today: two voluntary rak'ahs followed by the istikhara du'a, which the Prophet ﷺ taught his Companions for every matter (Bukhari 6382). Then move forward, trusting that Allah is guiding your steps.
day.13.quran.note: The well-known verse on trust: "And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose."
day.13.reflection: In which part of your life do you struggle most to trust Allah? What would happen if you truly let go?
day.13.sunnah.description: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ whether he should tie his camel and trust in Allah, or leave it untied and trust in Allah. He said: "Tie it, and trust in Allah." Tawakkul includes doing your part fully, then letting go of the outcome.
day.13.sunnah.title: Tie your camel first

day.14.character.action: Think of something that is difficult in your life right now. Write down 3 blessings that may be hidden in it.
day.14.character.description: Shukr trains us to see blessings even in hardship. Everything Allah decrees has wisdom, even what hurts.
day.14.dhikr.ainni_ala_dhikrik.meaning: (At the end of each prayer) O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You and worship You well
day.14.dhikr.hamdan_kathiran.meaning: (In prayer) Praise be to Allah, abundant, good and blessed praise
day.14.dhikr.waking_dua.meaning: (On waking) Praise be to Allah who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection
day.14.dhikr.waking_dua_afani.meaning: (On waking) Praise be to Allah who gave health to my body, returned my soul to me and permitted me to remember Him
day.14.hadith.meaning: "Look at those below you and do not look at those above you, for that is more fitting, so that you do not belittle the favours of Allah upon you."
day.14.intro: Allah says, "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you." Today, learn to see every moment as a gift from Him, and to show gratitude in word and deed.
day.14.prayer.tip: When good news or a blessing reaches you today, fall into a single prostration of gratitude (sujud ash-shukr). Whenever something pleasing came to the Prophet ﷺ, he would fall down in prostration, thanking Allah (Abu Dawud 2774). After each prayer, ask Allah to help you thank Him.
day.14.quran.note: Allah's promise that gratitude brings increase: "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe."
day.14.reflection: What is one blessing you often overlook or take for granted? How would your day change if you truly appreciated it?
day.14.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah." Show gratitude in two ways today: thank Allah directly (Alhamdulillah), and thank the people through whom He blessed you.
day.14.sunnah.title: Thank people too

day.15.character.action: Write an honest self-assessment: where do you fall short? What do you tell yourself that isn't fully true?
day.15.character.description: True sidq includes being honest with yourself about your flaws and weaknesses, without excuses or self-deception.
day.15.dhikr.astaghfirullah.meaning: I seek Allah's forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness a hundred times a day.
day.15.dhikr.ighsilni.meaning: (From the opening du'a of prayer) O Allah, wash away my sins with water, snow and hail
day.15.dhikr.sidq_dua.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, I ask You for truthfulness in speech and in action
day.15.hadith.meaning: "Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man keeps telling the truth until he becomes truthful. Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man keeps lying until he is written before Allah as a liar."
day.15.intro: Truthfulness in speech, in action and in the heart is the foundation of noble character. Today you practise complete honesty, with others and with yourself.
day.15.prayer.tip: Among the qualities Allah praises alongside truthfulness is seeking forgiveness before dawn (Al 'Imran 3:17). Tonight, pray 2 or more rak'ahs of night prayer, before you sleep or before Fajr, and ask Him for forgiveness.
day.15.quran.note: The command to stand with the truthful: "O you who believe, fear Allah and be with those who are truthful."
day.15.reflection: Is there an area where you have been less than fully honest, with others or with yourself?
day.15.sunnah.description: When the Prophet ﷺ called the tribes of Quraysh together, they told him: "We have never experienced anything from you but truthfulness." Today, be completely honest in every interaction: no white lies, exaggerations or misleading statements, even ones that seem harmless.
day.15.sunnah.title: No white lies or half-truths

day.16.character.action: Pick one unfulfilled promise or commitment. Fulfil it today, or speak honestly with the person involved.
day.16.character.description: Be the person people can count on. Your word is your bond: when you say you will do something, do it.
day.16.dhikr.audhu_minal_khiyanah.meanin: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hunger, for it is a wretched bed-fellow, and from treachery, for it is a wretched inner companion
day.16.dhikr.subhanallahil_azimi_wa_biha: Glory be to Allah the Magnificent, and praise be to Him
day.16.hadith.meaning: "Indeed, each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock."
day.16.intro: Amanah means fulfilling trusts, keeping promises and being reliable in every role: in your family, with friends, at work and as a Muslim. Even before prophethood, the Prophet ﷺ was known among his people for his trustworthiness.
day.16.prayer.tip: Prayer itself is a trust from Allah. Fulfil it completely today: pray all 5 prayers on time, with their sunnah rak'ahs, with good wudu, facing the qiblah.
day.16.quran.note: "O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, and do not knowingly betray your trusts."
day.16.reflection: Who and what has been placed in your care? In which of those roles could you be more trustworthy or reliable?
day.16.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks his promise, and when he is trusted he betrays the trust." List any promises or commitments you have not kept, and fulfil at least one today.
day.16.sunnah.title: Keeping promises

day.17.character.action: When you feel irritated or frustrated today, stop and say "Alhamdulillah 'ala kulli hal" (praise be to Allah in every situation) before you respond.
day.17.character.description: Sabr in the face of anger, frustration and difficulty is the highest level of this quality.
day.17.dhikr.audhu_minal_jaza.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, I seek refuge in You from panic and despair in hardship
day.17.dhikr.istirja.meaning: (At a calamity) We belong to Allah and to Him we return. O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with something better
day.17.dhikr.sabr_dua.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, I ask You for patience with what You decree
day.17.dhikr.subhanallahi_wa_bihamdihi.m: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him
day.17.hadith.meaning: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer! All of it is good, and that is for no one except the believer. If something good happens to him, he is grateful, and that is good for him. If something bad happens to him, he is patient, and that is good for him."
day.17.intro: "Indeed, Allah is with the patient." Sabr is not passive resignation; it is active, disciplined perseverance, knowing that Allah is testing and refining you.
day.17.prayer.tip: Fajr is itself a test of sabr: leaving sleep and a warm bed. Today, when the alarm rings, practise patience by getting up straight away. Each morning is training in sabr.
day.17.quran.note: Allah tests us with fear, hunger and loss, "but give good tidings to the patient: those who, when disaster strikes them, say: Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return."
day.17.reflection: What tests you most in life right now? How can you see it as something Allah is using to raise you?
day.17.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The strong one is not the one who overcomes people by his strength, but the one who controls himself when angry." When something irritates you today, pause and say "A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim" (Bukhari 6115). If you are standing, sit down (Abu Dawud 4782).
day.17.sunnah.title: Patience in anger

day.18.character.action: Sincerely praise someone's work or quality today without comparing them to yourself. Celebrate someone else's success.
day.18.character.description: Pride (kibr) is a disease of the heart. The Prophet ﷺ said that no one with an atom's weight of pride in his heart will enter Paradise, and he defined pride as "rejecting the truth and looking down on people" (Muslim 91).
day.18.dhikr.audhu_minal_kibr.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, I seek refuge in You from arrogance and self-admiration
day.18.dhikr.kaffarat_al_majlis.meaning: (At the end of a sitting) Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise; I testify there is no god but You; I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You
day.18.hadith.meaning: "Allah has revealed to me that you must be humble towards one another, so that no one boasts over another and no one wrongs another."
day.18.intro: The Prophet ﷺ was the most humble of people, though he was the greatest of them. True tawadu' comes from knowing Allah and knowing yourself.
day.18.prayer.tip: Placing your forehead on the ground is the fullest physical expression of humility. In every sujood today, say "Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la" (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High; Muslim 772) and feel its meaning: you are submitting completely to Him. Let that feeling stay with you.
day.18.quran.note: "And do not walk upon the earth arrogantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, and you will never reach the mountains in height."
day.18.reflection: In which situations do you feel superior to others? How can you grow real humility in those moments?
day.18.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ would greet even children with salam (Bukhari 6247; Muslim 2168), and he said: "The people closest to Allah are those who begin the greeting of salam." Today, be the first to say salam to everyone you meet.
day.18.sunnah.title: Be the first to give salam

day.19.character.action: Reach out to someone you know who is struggling. Not to advise them, just to listen and show you care.
day.19.character.description: True rahmah means feeling the pain of others and acting to relieve it, without judging their struggles.
day.19.dhikr.basmalah.meaning: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
day.19.dhikr.ighfir_lil_muminin.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, forgive the believing men and women
day.19.dhikr.irhamna_bi_rahmatik.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, have mercy on us with Your mercy that encompasses all things
day.19.dhikr.rabbana_wasita.meaning: Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire
day.19.hadith.meaning: "The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One above the heavens will have mercy on you."
day.19.intro: The Prophet ﷺ was sent as a mercy to all the worlds. Mercy towards people, animals and all of creation is a sign of strong faith.
day.19.prayer.tip: In today's prayers, make specific du'a for others: your parents, your family, the sick and suffering, and Muslims around the world. The Prophet ﷺ said that when a believer prays for his brother in his absence, the angel says, "And the same for you" (Muslim 2732).
day.19.quran.note: The summary of the Prophet's ﷺ mission: "And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds."
day.19.reflection: Who in your life needs more mercy and compassion from you? How can you show it this week?
day.19.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ told of a woman who entered the Fire because of a cat she locked up without food or water, and of a man who gave water to a thirsty dog, so Allah thanked him and admitted him to Paradise. Today, show active mercy: feed a bird, put out water, be gentle with animals and reduce waste.
day.19.sunnah.title: Mercy to animals

day.2.character.action: Whenever you feel the urge to speak badly about someone, say "SubhanAllah" instead and change the topic.
day.2.character.description: Purity includes our words. Today, stay away from backbiting, lying and idle talk.
day.2.dhikr.kaffarat_al_majlis.meaning: (At the end of a sitting) Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise; I testify there is no god but You; I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You
day.2.dhikr.sayyid_istighfar.meaning: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and my promise to You as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
day.2.dhikr.shahadah_after_wudu.meaning: (After wudu) I testify that there is no god but Allah, alone without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger
day.2.dhikr.subhanallahi_wa_bihamdihi.me: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him
day.2.intro: Islam cares for both outward and inward cleanliness. Today you learn that purity is the key to prayer and the foundation of worship.
day.2.prayer.dua.meaning: (After the shahadah that follows wudu) O Allah, make me among those who repent and make me among those who purify themselves.
day.2.prayer.tip: Make each wudu today carefully: begin with Bismillah, follow the order, wash each part well, and say the shahadah when you finish. You may also add this du'a.
day.2.quran.note: Reflect on this verse about purification: "Indeed, Allah loves those who turn to Him in repentance and loves those who purify themselves."
day.2.reflection: In which parts of your life (physical, spiritual or social) do you most need purification?
day.2.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Were it not that it would be hard on my ummah, I would have commanded them to use the siwak with every prayer." Use a siwak or brush your teeth before your prayers today.
day.2.sunnah.title: Siwak or careful brushing

day.20.character.action: If there is a rift in any family relationship, take the first step today to repair it, even with a simple kind message.
day.20.character.description: Family conflicts are inevitable. The question is whether you hold grudges or choose to forgive for the sake of Allah.
day.20.dhikr.barik_li_fi_ahli.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, bless me in my family and my wealth
day.20.dhikr.ijma_shamla_ahli.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, unite my family in obeying You
day.20.dhikr.subhanallahi_wa_bihamdihi.m: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him
day.20.hadith.meaning: "Whoever loves that his provision be expanded and his life be extended, let him keep the ties of kinship."
day.20.intro: Keeping family ties is one of the most emphasised duties in Islam, and cutting them is a serious sin. Today, actively strengthen your bonds with your family.
day.20.prayer.tip: After Fajr, call or message a family member you haven't spoken to recently, so your day begins with keeping ties.
day.20.quran.note: Allah links keeping family ties directly to fearing Him: "And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs."
day.20.reflection: Which family relationships need your attention and repair? What small step can you take today?
day.20.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The one who keeps ties is not the one who only returns the favour, but the one who keeps ties when they have been cut." Today, reach out to a family member you have drifted away from.
day.20.sunnah.title: Keeping ties even when others don't

day.21.character.action: Speak kindly and warmly to every person today. Go out of your way to say something encouraging to at least 3 people.
day.21.character.description: The Prophet ﷺ said that a good word is charity (Bukhari 2989; Muslim 1009). The words you choose can lift people up or tear them down, so choose every word with care today.
day.21.dhikr.ahsanta_khalqi.meaning: O Allah, You have made my form beautiful, so make my character beautiful
day.21.dhikr.astaghfirullah.meaning: I seek Allah's forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness a hundred times a day.
day.21.dhikr.ihdini_li_ahsanil_akhlaq.me: (From a longer du'a) And guide me to the best of character, for none guides to the best of it but You; and turn away from me its evil, for none turns away its evil but You
day.21.hadith.meaning: "Indeed, among the best of you are those with the best character."
day.21.intro: Nothing is heavier on the believer's scale on the Day of Resurrection than good character (Abu Dawud 4799; Tirmidhi 2002). Today you consciously practise beautiful manners in every interaction.
day.21.prayer.tip: Pray each salah today with softness and calm, and let the sweetness of the prayer carry into how you treat people afterwards.
day.21.quran.note: Allah's description of the Prophet ﷺ: "And indeed, you are of a great moral character."
day.21.reflection: Who in your life deserves more kindness and patience from you? How has your character grown over these 21 days?
day.21.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you." Jarir said that from the day he accepted Islam, the Prophet ﷺ never saw him without smiling at him. Today, smile genuinely at every person you meet: at home, at work and in the street.
day.21.sunnah.title: The smile

day.22.character.action: Read one article or listen to one Islamic lecture today. Write down 3 things you learned.
day.22.character.description: The more you learn, the more you realise how little you know. True scholars are the most humble.
day.22.dhikr.ilman_nafian.meaning: (After the salam of Fajr) O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision and accepted deeds
day.22.dhikr.rabbi_zidni_ilma.meaning: (From Quran 20:114, where Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to say it) My Lord, increase me in knowledge
day.22.dhikr.subhanallahi_wa_bihamdihi.m: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him
day.22.hadith.meaning: "Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise."
day.22.intro: Knowledge of the deen is the light by which you worship Allah as He deserves. Today you rekindle the pursuit of 'ilm as an act of worship.
day.22.prayer.tip: After Fajr, while the mind is fresh and the world is quiet, spend 15 minutes studying one Islamic topic. Begin with the du'a for beneficial knowledge that the Prophet ﷺ said after the salam of Fajr.
day.22.quran.note: Scholars note that knowledge is the only thing the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to ask for more of: "And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge."
day.22.reflection: What gaps in your Islamic knowledge cause you the most uncertainty in your daily life?
day.22.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding of the religion." Learn one new thing about your deen today: a ruling of fiqh, a name of Allah, a hadith or the tafsir of an ayah.

day.23.character.action: Spend 15 minutes in complete silence today. No phone, no noise: just you, your thoughts and Allah.
day.23.character.description: In a world of constant distraction, the ability to think deeply about life's real questions is increasingly rare, and precious.
day.23.dhikr.rabbana_ma_khalaqta.meaning: Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire
(Three times, after Fajr) Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, as many times as the number of His creation, as much as pleases Him, as much as the weight of His Throne, and as much as the ink of His words
day.23.hadith.meaning: Ibn 'Abbas said that when it was the last third of the night, the Prophet ﷺ sat up, looked at the sky and recited: "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding" (3:190).
day.23.intro: Allah repeatedly calls us to reflect on His creation and on ourselves. Today, step back from the rush of life and contemplate the signs of Allah.
day.23.prayer.tip: If you can, pray at least one prayer outdoors today: on a balcony, in a garden or at a park. Let the creation around you remind you of the Creator.
day.23.quran.note: The people of understanding remember Allah standing, sitting and lying down, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth.
day.23.reflection: What in creation most fills you with a sense of Allah's greatness? The stars? The human body? The ocean?
day.23.sunnah.description: Allah praises those who "reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth" and say: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain." Take 15 minutes outside today: walk, sit and look at the sky, and say "SubhanAllah" at each sign of creation you notice.
day.23.sunnah.title: Reflecting on creation

day.24.character.action: Identify one thing you own or one habit you have that is more hindrance than benefit to your deen. Consider reducing it.
day.24.character.description: Before every major decision, ask: "How does this serve my akhirah?" Let that question reframe your choices.
day.24.dhikr.asalukal_jannah.meaning: (From a longer du'a) O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and for whatever word or deed brings me near to it
day.24.dhikr.la_tajal_ad_dunya.meaning: (From a longer du'a he often made before rising from a gathering) And do not make this world our greatest concern nor the limit of our knowledge
day.24.hadith.meaning: "Be in this world as if you were a stranger or a traveller."
day.24.intro: Zuhd does not mean poverty; it means your heart is not enslaved to worldly things. You use the world, but your heart lives for the akhirah.
day.24.prayer.tip: A sign of zuhd is giving your time to prayer over worldly pursuits. Today, pray the sunnah prayers with each fard: the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever prays twelve rak'ahs in a day and night, a house is built for him in Paradise (Muslim 728).
day.24.quran.note: The parable of this world: "Know that the life of this world is but amusement and diversion and adornment and boasting to one another and competition in increase of wealth and children..."
day.24.reflection: Which worldly attachment (money, status, entertainment or comfort) has the strongest grip on your heart?
day.24.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "There are two blessings that many people are cheated of: health and free time." Today, take a 3-hour break from social media and entertainment, and use that time for worship instead.
day.24.sunnah.title: A digital detox

day.25.character.action: Do one significant act of worship today that only you and Allah know about. No telling, no posting, no hints.
day.25.character.description: Among the seven whom Allah will shade on the Day when there is no shade but His is "a man who gives charity so secretly that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives" (Bukhari 660; Muslim 1031).
day.25.dhikr.audhu_an_ushrika.meaning: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowingly associating anything with You, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know
day.25.dhikr.umar_dua_ikhlas.meaning: (Du'a of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab) O Allah, make all my deeds righteous, purely for Your Face, and let no one have any share in them
day.25.hadith.meaning: "Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."
day.25.intro: Sincerity is the soul of all worship: a deed is only accepted when it is done for Allah alone. Today you examine and purify your intentions.
day.25.prayer.tip: Before each prayer today, check your intention: "Am I praying because people might see me, or purely for Allah?" Let every rak'ah be for Him alone.
day.25.quran.note: The essence of the religion: "And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakah. And that is the correct religion."
day.25.reflection: Which of your acts of worship might be tainted by the desire for praise or recognition?
day.25.sunnah.description: Allah says in a hadith qudsi: "I am the most free of need of any partner. Whoever does a deed in which he associates anyone else with Me, I leave him and his association." Test each action today: "Would I do this the same way if no one was watching?" If not, correct your intention.
day.25.sunnah.title: The showing-off test

day.26.character.action: Today, behave exactly the same whether or not you think you are being observed.
day.26.character.description: Who are you when no one is watching? Muraqabah means your private self and your public self are one and the same.
day.26.dhikr.sayyid_istighfar.meaning: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and my promise to You as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
day.26.dhikr.subhanallahi_wa_bihamdihi.m: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him
day.26.dhikr.yuraqibuka.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, make me among those who are mindful of You in private and in public
day.26.hadith.meaning: "[Ihsan is] to worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He surely sees you."
day.26.intro: Muraqabah is living with the awareness that Allah sees your actions, your words and your secret thoughts. It is the heart of ihsan, the highest level of worship.
day.26.prayer.tip: Bring the awareness that Allah sees you into every rak'ah today, from the opening takbir to the final salam.
day.26.quran.note: "And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing."
day.26.reflection: How would your behaviour change if you were always aware that Allah sees you? What would you stop doing, and what would you start?
day.26.sunnah.description: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Hold yourselves to account before you are held to account." This is a saying of 'Umar, not a hadith. Before sleeping, review your day: what did you do well, where did you fall short, and what will you improve tomorrow?
day.26.sunnah.title: Muhasabah (self-accounting)

day.27.character.action: Make a list of 5 specific things you want to change or improve for good. These become your commitments after the 30 days.
day.27.character.description: Real tawbah takes the courage to admit wrongdoing honestly and commit to change, even when it is uncomfortable.
day.27.dhikr.asalukal_afiyah.meaning: (Morning and evening) O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the next. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly life, my family and my wealth. O Allah, cover my faults and calm my fears. O Allah, guard me from in front, behind, my right, my left and above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being struck down from beneath me
day.27.dhikr.astaghfirullah_al_azim.mean: I seek forgiveness from Allah the Magnificent, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer, and I repent to Him
day.27.dhikr.rabbana_zalamna.meaning: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers
day.27.hadith.meaning: "Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one of you who comes upon his camel after losing it in a desolate land."
day.27.intro: Tawbah nasuha is sincere repentance: real remorse, leaving the sin, and resolving never to return to it. Today you make a deep spiritual cleanse before the final days.
day.27.prayer.tip: In the last third of tonight, when Allah descends to the lowest heaven and asks, "Who is seeking My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?" (Bukhari 1145), pray tahajjud and make the most sincere tawbah of your life. Be specific about what you are repenting from.
day.27.quran.note: The command to repent sincerely: "O you who believe, turn to Allah in sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow."
day.27.reflection: What is the one thing you most need to change about yourself? Are you ready to make that change for good?
day.27.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "No servant commits a sin, then purifies himself well, stands and prays two rak'ahs, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, except that Allah forgives him." Then he recited Al 'Imran 3:135. Make wudu carefully today, pray two rak'ahs and ask Allah to forgive you.
day.27.sunnah.title: Two rak'ahs of repentance (Salat at-Tawbah)

day.28.character.action: Make du'a for 5 specific Muslims by name today, living and deceased, and feel the bond of the ummah in that du'a.
day.28.character.description: True brotherhood in Islam means feeling the pain of your brothers and sisters, not just knowing them.
day.28.dhikr.aslih_ummata_muhammad.meani: (Personal du'a) O Allah, set right the ummah of Muhammad, relieve the ummah of Muhammad, and have mercy on the ummah of Muhammad
day.28.dhikr.subhanallahi_wa_bihamdihi.m: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him
day.28.dhikr.unsur_al_islam.meaning: (Personal du'a) O Allah, give victory to Islam and the Muslims
day.28.hadith.meaning: "The believer to the believer is like a building, each part strengthening the other."
day.28.intro: The Prophet ﷺ likened the believers, in their mercy and affection for one another, to one body (Bukhari 6011; Muslim 2586). Today you invest in your community.
day.28.prayer.tip: If it is Friday, attend Jumu'ah. If not, pray at least one fard prayer in congregation at the masjid today: prayer in congregation is twenty-seven degrees better than praying alone (Bukhari 645).
day.28.quran.note: "You are the best nation produced for mankind. You enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah."
day.28.reflection: How can you serve your local Muslim community more actively in the next 30 days?
day.28.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever fulfils the need of his brother, Allah will fulfil his need; and whoever relieves a Muslim of a hardship, Allah will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection." Today, volunteer, help a neighbour, contribute to a community cause or visit a sick Muslim.

day.29.character.action: Share one beneficial Islamic reminder or piece of knowledge with someone today: a family member, friend or colleague.
day.29.character.description: You don't need to give lectures to do da'wah. Share an Islamic reminder, or simply tell someone one beautiful thing about your deen.
day.29.dhikr.hudatan_muhtadin.meaning: (From a longer du'a) O Allah, adorn us with the beauty of faith, and make us guides who are themselves rightly guided
day.29.dhikr.salawat_ibrahimiyyah.meanin: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
day.29.hadith.meaning: "Convey from me, even if it is one verse."
day.29.intro: Every Muslim represents the deen, and da'wah is not only for scholars: it is living Islam so beautifully that others are inspired. "And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah?"
day.29.prayer.tip: In your prayers today, make heartfelt du'a by name for people who are not Muslim or who have drifted from Islam. The Prophet ﷺ prayed for people's guidance: "O Allah, guide Daws" (Bukhari 2937), and he prayed for the guidance of Abu Hurayrah's mother (Muslim 2491).
day.29.quran.note: "And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah, does righteousness and says: Indeed, I am of the Muslims."
day.29.reflection: Who in your life most needs a connection to Islam or to Allah? How can you be a bridge for them?
day.29.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "That Allah guides one person through you is better for you than red camels." The greatest da'wah is your character: when you are kind, honest, reliable, generous and humble, people see Islam in action. Embody these qualities in every interaction today.

day.3.character.action: Plan your day around the prayer times instead of fitting prayer into your day.
day.3.character.description: Prayer teaches discipline: showing up at set times whatever your mood or schedule.
day.3.dhikr.alhamdulillah.meaning: (After each prayer) All praise is for Allah
day.3.dhikr.allahuakbar.meaning: (After each prayer) Allah is the Greatest
day.3.dhikr.dua_after_adhan.meaning: (After each adhan) O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and the prayer about to be established, grant Muhammad al-Wasilah and excellence, and raise him to the praised station You promised him
day.3.dhikr.subhanallah.meaning: (After each prayer) Glory be to Allah
day.3.dhikr.tahlil.meaning: (The 100th, after the tasbih) None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things
day.3.dhikr.waking_dua.meaning: (On waking) Praise be to Allah who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection
day.3.hadith.meaning: "The first of his deeds for which a servant will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection is his prayer. If it is sound, he has succeeded and prospered; if it is corrupt, he has failed and lost."
day.3.intro: Prayer is the pillar of Islam. Today you aim to pray all five prayers on time, aware that you are standing before Allah.
day.3.prayer.tip: Pray each prayer soon after the adhan today. Set an alarm for each prayer time. Before you begin, take a moment to quiet your mind and remember that you are about to stand before your Creator.
day.3.quran.note: "Guard your prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion." Reflect on what it means to truly guard your prayers.
day.3.reflection: What keeps you from praying on time? How can you remove those obstacles for good?
day.3.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever prays twelve voluntary rak'ahs in a day and night, a house will be built for him in Paradise. They are 2 before Fajr, 4 before Dhuhr and 2 after it, 2 after Maghrib and 2 after Isha.

day.30.character.action: Write your covenant with Allah: your personal commitment to the acts of worship and qualities of character you will keep for life.
day.30.character.description: Today is not an ending; it is a beginning. Your 30 days have built habits, and now they must become your way of life.
day.30.dhikr.ighfir_li_ma_qaddamtu.meani: O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I have left for later, what I did in secret and what I did openly, and what You know better than I. You are the One who brings forward and the One who puts back, and You are able to do all things
day.30.dhikr.musarrifal_qulub.meaning: O Allah, Director of hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience
day.30.dhikr.ya_muqallibal_qulub.meaning: (Umm Salamah said this was the du'a he made most often when he was with her) O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion
day.30.hadith.meaning: "Say: I believe in Allah, then be steadfast." (His answer to Sufyan ibn 'Abdullah ath-Thaqafi, who asked for a teaching he would never need to ask anyone else about.)
day.30.intro: You have reached Day 30, but the journey does not end here; it begins here. Istiqamah means staying on the straight path consistently, as the Prophet ﷺ taught: "Say: I believe in Allah, then be steadfast."
day.30.prayer.tip: Make today a complete day of prayer: the five fard prayers, the twelve sunnah rak'ahs (Muslim 728), Duha in the morning and tahajjud tonight. Let it be the high point of your 30-day prayer journey.
day.30.quran.note: The promise to those who remain steadfast: "Indeed, those who say, Our Lord is Allah, and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them: Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised."
day.30.reflection: Looking back over 30 days: what has changed in you? What is your covenant with Allah from here on?
day.30.sunnah.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The most beloved of deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small." Plan a daily routine of prayer, Quran, dhikr and character work for the next 30 days that you can keep up.

day.4.character.action: Make a firm intention tonight to wake for Fajr each day of this path, and write it down.
day.4.character.description: Commitment means showing up even when it is hard. Fajr tests it like nothing else.
day.4.dhikr.asbahna_ala_fitrah.meaning: We have entered the morning upon the natural way of Islam, the word of sincerity, the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the way of our father Ibrahim, upright and submitting, who was not of the polytheists
day.4.dhikr.audhu_bikalimatillah.meaning: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created
day.4.dhikr.bika_amsayna.meaning: O Allah, by You we enter the evening and by You we enter the morning, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the final return
day.4.dhikr.bika_asbahna.meaning: O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection
day.4.hadith.meaning: "Whoever prays Subh (Fajr) is under the protection of Allah."
day.4.intro: Fajr is a special meeting with Allah: rising in the quiet of dawn to stand before Him while the world sleeps. If it is hard for you, every step toward it counts.
day.4.prayer.dua.meaning: O Allah, place light in my heart, light in my tongue, light in my hearing and light in my sight.
day.4.prayer.tip: Sleep early tonight and lay out your prayer mat before bed. When the alarm rings, sit up straight away and say the waking du'a, "Al-hamdu lillahil-ladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur." Don't lie back down; wudu will wake you fully.
day.4.quran.note: Read about the dawn prayer, which the angels witness: "Indeed, the recitation at dawn is ever witnessed."
day.4.reflection: How does it feel to rise before the world and stand before your Creator in the quiet of dawn?
day.4.sunnah.description: On waking, say the waking du'a, wipe the sleep from your face with your hand, make wudu, and pray the 2 sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than this world and everything in it."

day.5.character.action: Be fully present in 3 conversations today: put your phone away, make eye contact and truly listen.
day.5.character.description: Being present in prayer trains you to be present in life, and it carries over into how you treat people.
day.5.dhikr.dua_dhun_nun.meaning: There is no god but You, glory be to You; I have been among the wrongdoers
day.5.dhikr.salawat.meaning: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad
day.5.dhikr.subhanallahil_azim.meaning: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; glory be to Allah the Magnificent
day.5.dhikr.ya_hayyu_ya_qayyum.meaning: (In times of distress) O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek help
day.5.hadith.meaning: "Pray as you have seen me praying."
day.5.intro: Khushu' is the heart being present with Allah in prayer; it is the soul of salah. Without it the body prays while the heart is elsewhere.
day.5.prayer.dua.meaning: (In ruku' and sujood) Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me.
day.5.prayer.tip: Before Dhuhr, remind yourself that you are about to speak to Allah. Slow every movement and make your ruku' and sujood longer than usual. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is in prostration, so make much du'a."
day.5.quran.note: The first quality of the successful believers is khushu' in prayer: "Successful indeed are the believers, those who are humble in their prayer."
day.5.reflection: When did you last feel truly close to Allah in prayer? What made that moment special?
day.5.sunnah.description: Make your prostration longer than usual today. In sujood, repeat "Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la" (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High), then make your own du'a. In his night prayer, the Prophet's ﷺ prostration lasted as long as it takes to recite fifty verses.

day.6.character.action: Choose a fixed daily Quran time, even 10 minutes, and protect it.
day.6.character.description: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The most beloved of deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small" (Bukhari 6464). A small daily Quran habit shapes the soul over time.
day.6.dhikr.ihdini_li_ahsanil_akhlaq.mea: (From a longer du'a) And guide me to the best of character, for none guides to the best of it but You; and turn away from me its evil, for none turns away its evil but You
day.6.dhikr.rabi_qalbi.meaning: (From a longer du'a for distress, Ahmad 3712) O Allah, make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the remover of my sorrow and the reliever of my distress
day.6.dhikr.subhanallahi_wa_bihamdihi.me: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him
day.6.hadith.meaning: "Whoever reads a letter from the Book of Allah receives a good deed for it, and a good deed is multiplied ten times. I do not say that Alif-Lam-Mim is one letter; rather Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter and Mim is a letter."
day.6.intro: The Quran is the speech of Allah, and a daily Quran habit is one of the most powerful things a Muslim can build. Today you begin a lifelong bond with the Book of Allah.
day.6.prayer.tip: Read some Quran around Isha or before bed tonight. Even 5 to 10 minutes is a blessed habit. Recite slowly and with care; quality matters more than quantity.
day.6.quran.note: Read the opening of Al-Baqarah. It describes the people of taqwa: they believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend from what they are given.
day.6.reflection: What Quran goal would you like to reach by the end of this year? How will you shape your daily recitation?
day.6.sunnah.description: Set a fixed time each day for the Quran. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it." Even one verse read with reflection is valuable. Start small and stay consistent.

day.7.character.action: Write down anything weighing on your conscience, then sincerely seek forgiveness for each one.
day.7.character.description: Never despair of Allah's mercy. No sin is too great for His forgiveness, and sincere repentance wipes the slate clean.
day.7.dhikr.astaghfirullah_al_azim.meani: I seek forgiveness from Allah the Magnificent, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer, and I repent to Him
day.7.dhikr.sayyid_istighfar.meaning: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and my promise to You as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
day.7.hadith.meaning: "By Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day."
day.7.intro: The door of repentance is always open, and Allah loves those who return to Him. Today, turn back to Him sincerely, let go of the weight of past sins, and begin fresh.
day.7.prayer.dua.meaning: O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in this world and the Hereafter.
day.7.prayer.tip: Tonight, before you sleep or in the last part of the night before Fajr, pray 2 or more rak'ahs of night prayer. Ask Allah sincerely for forgiveness. Allah descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of the night and asks, "Who is asking Me for forgiveness, that I may forgive him?" (Bukhari 1145)
day.7.quran.note: One of the most hopeful verses in the Quran: "Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins."
day.7.reflection: What sins or regrets have been weighing on your heart? How does knowing that Allah forgives all sins make you feel?
day.7.sunnah.description: Say the master du'a of seeking forgiveness in the morning and the evening. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever says it with certainty during the day and dies before evening, or says it at night and dies before morning, is of the people of Paradise.
day.7.sunnah.title: Sayyid al-Istighfar

day.8.character.action: Name 10 specific blessings today. Be specific: not just "health" but "I can see, I have food, I have a home."
day.8.character.description: Dhikr trains the heart in gratitude. When you remember Allah often, you notice His countless blessings.
day.8.dhikr.afini_fi_badani.meaning: O Allah, grant me well-being in my body, my hearing and my sight; there is no god but You
day.8.dhikr.amsayna_wa_amsal_mulk.meanin: We have entered the evening and the dominion belongs to Allah; praise be to Allah; none has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and the praise, and He is able to do all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and what follows it, and seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and in the grave
day.8.dhikr.bismillah_alladhi.meaning: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing
day.8.dhikr.hasbiyallah.meaning: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him; in Him I trust, and He is Lord of the Mighty Throne
day.8.dhikr.three_quls.meaning: Surahs Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas, three times each in the morning and evening. The Prophet ﷺ said they will suffice you against everything.
day.8.hadith.meaning: "The example of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not is like the living and the dead."
day.8.intro: Remembrance of Allah nourishes the heart: "Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest." Today you build a morning and evening dhikr routine to carry with you every day.
day.8.prayer.tip: After Maghrib tonight, don't rush away. Stay seated and say the evening adhkar before you get up.
day.8.quran.note: The well-known verse about dhikr and the heart: "Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest."
day.8.reflection: How does your heart feel before and after sincere dhikr?
day.8.sunnah.description: Begin learning the morning and evening adhkar. Today, at the least, recite the three Quls (Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas) three times each, morning and evening, and the tasbih after your prayers (33 + 33 + 33, then the tahlil) (Muslim 597). Recite Ayat al-Kursi before you sleep (Bukhari 2311).

day.9.character.description: Love for the Prophet ﷺ grows and shows as you follow his way. Every Sunnah you follow is a sign of it.
day.9.dhikr.salawat.meaning: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad
day.9.dhikr.salawat_ibrahimiyyah.meaning: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
day.9.hadith.meaning: "None of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child and all of mankind."
day.9.intro: Following the Sunnah means living as the Prophet ﷺ lived. Every Sunnah you revive is an act of love for him and a source of great reward.
day.9.prayer.tip: Today, focus on praying as the Prophet ﷺ prayed. Learn one Sunnah of prayer you may have missed, such as the opening du'a (istiftah), the du'a between the two prostrations, or a du'a in the final tashahhud.
day.9.quran.note: The verse that makes the Prophet ﷺ our finest example: "There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example."
day.9.reflection: Which Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ do you most want to make a permanent part of your life?
day.9.sunnah.description: Today, practise the Sunnah of eating: say Bismillah, eat with your right hand and from what is in front of you (Bukhari 5376; Muslim 2022); never criticise food (Bukhari 5409; Muslim 2064); lick your fingers when you finish (Muslim 2031); and praise Allah afterwards (Muslim 2734).

dua.before_eating.meaning: In the name of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ told a boy: “Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.”

dua.before_sleeping.meaning: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

learn.dua_after_wudu.meaning: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. (Whoever performs wudu well, then says this, the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him.)
learn.evening_adhkar.afiyah.meaning: O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the next. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly life, my family and my wealth. O Allah, cover my faults and calm my fears. O Allah, guard me from in front, behind, my right, my left and above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being struck down from beneath me.
learn.evening_adhkar.alimal_ghayb.meanin: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things: I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own self and from the evil of Shaytan and his call to shirk.
learn.evening_adhkar.amsayna_wa_amsal_mu: We have entered the evening and the dominion belongs to Allah; praise be to Allah; none has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and the praise, and He is able to do all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and what follows it, and seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and in the grave.
learn.evening_adhkar.audhu_bikalimatilla: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created.
learn.evening_adhkar.ayat_al_kursi.meani: Allah: there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Who could intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they grasp nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and guarding them does not tire Him. He is the Most High, the Magnificent.

learn.evening_adhkar.surah_falaq.meaning: Al-Falaq: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak, from the evil of what He created, from the evil of darkness when it settles, from the evil of those who blow on knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies.
learn.evening_adhkar.surah_ikhlas.meanin: Al-Ikhlas: Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Self-Sufficient on whom all depend. He neither begets nor was He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.
learn.evening_adhkar.surah_nas.meaning: An-Nas: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer, who whispers into the hearts of mankind, from among jinn and mankind.

learn.pillar.allah.meaning: Believing that Allah exists, that He alone is Lord and alone deserves worship, and in His names and attributes.
learn.pillar.allah.name: Belief in Allah
learn.pillar.angels.meaning: Believing in the angels, created from light, who always obey Allah, such as Jibril.
learn.pillar.angels.name: Belief in the angels
learn.pillar.books.meaning: Believing in the books Allah revealed, such as the Torah and the Gospel, with the Quran as the final, preserved one.
learn.pillar.books.name: Belief in the books
learn.pillar.hajj.meaning: Pilgrimage to the Ka‘bah once in a lifetime, for those who are able.
learn.pillar.hajj.name: Hajj
learn.pillar.last_day.meaning: Believing in what comes after death: the grave, the resurrection, the judgement, Paradise and Hell.
learn.pillar.last_day.name: Belief in the Last Day
learn.pillar.messengers.meaning: Believing in all of Allah's messengers, from Nuh to Muhammad ﷺ, the last of them.
learn.pillar.messengers.name: Belief in the messengers
learn.pillar.qadar.meaning: Believing that everything, good and bad, happens by Allah's knowledge, writing, will and creation.
learn.pillar.qadar.name: Belief in the divine decree
learn.pillar.salah.meaning: Establishing the five daily prayers on time.
learn.pillar.salah.name: Salah
learn.pillar.sawm.meaning: Fasting from dawn to sunset throughout the month of Ramadan.
learn.pillar.sawm.name: Fasting Ramadan
learn.pillar.shahadah.meaning: Testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
learn.pillar.shahadah.name: Shahadah

learn.pillar.zakah.name: Zakah
learn.salah_notes.aloud_or_silent.body: Fajr is recited aloud, and so are the first two rak'ahs of Maghrib and Isha. Dhuhr and Asr are recited silently. "Aloud" applies to men and to the imam; for women, see the note below.
learn.salah_notes.aloud_or_silent.title: Aloud or silent
learn.salah_notes.for_women.body: During menstruation and post-natal bleeding a woman does not pray, and she does not make up those prayers afterwards (Bukhari 321; Muslim 335). When non-mahram men are present, recite so that only you can hear. In prayer, cover the whole body except the face and hands.
learn.salah_notes.for_women.title: For women
learn.salah_notes.madhhab_details.body: The four schools (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali) differ on a few details, such as where the hands rest, raising the hands at ruku‘, how you sit, and reciting Al-Fatihah behind an imam. Follow one trusted teacher or madhhab; every one of these ways is valid.
learn.salah_notes.madhhab_details.title: Small differences between madhhabs
learn.salah_notes.three_four_rakahs.body: After the second rak'ah, sit and recite the tashahhud only up to "ʿabduhū wa rasūluh" (Shafi'is also add the salawat), then stand with Allahu akbar. In the 3rd and 4th rak'ahs recite only Al-Fatihah, silently, then finish with the full final sitting and the salam.
learn.salah_steps.salah_fatihah.body: Recite Al-Fatihah, then say Āmīn. The Prophet ﷺ said there is no prayer without it (Bukhari 756).
learn.salah_steps.salah_fatihah.recite.m: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is for Allah, Lord of all the worlds, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who earned Your anger, nor of those who went astray.
learn.salah_steps.salah_fatihah.title: Recite Al-Fatihah
learn.salah_steps.salah_final_dua.body: Before the salam, seek refuge in Allah from these four things, then ask Him for whatever you need.
learn.salah_steps.salah_final_dua.recite: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the False Messiah.
learn.salah_steps.salah_final_dua.title: A du‘a before ending
learn.salah_steps.salah_istiadhah.body: Quietly seek refuge in Allah before you recite.
learn.salah_steps.salah_istiadhah.recite: I seek refuge in Allah from Shaytan, the accursed.
learn.salah_steps.salah_istiadhah.title: Seek refuge
learn.salah_steps.salah_opening_dua.body: Quietly say this short opening du‘a. It is sunnah, so your prayer is still valid while you are learning it.
learn.salah_steps.salah_opening_dua.reci: Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise; blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.
learn.salah_steps.salah_prepare.body: Make wudu, cover yourself properly and face the qiblah. Intend in your heart which prayer you are praying (for example, Fajr, 2 rak'ahs); nothing needs to be said aloud.
learn.salah_steps.salah_prepare.title: Get ready
learn.salah_steps.salah_rising.body: Rise saying the first phrase, then once you are standing straight say the second. In most schools, behind an imam say only the second phrase (Shafi'is say both).
learn.salah_steps.salah_rising.recite.me: Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise.
learn.salah_steps.salah_rising.title: Stand back up
learn.salah_steps.salah_ruku.body: Say Allahu akbar and bow with your back straight and hands on your knees, and be still. Say this; once is valid, and it is commonly said three times.
learn.salah_steps.salah_ruku.recite.mean: Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent
learn.salah_steps.salah_ruku.title: Bow (ruku‘)
learn.salah_steps.salah_salawat.body: Still sitting, send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ.
learn.salah_steps.salah_salawat.recite.m: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
learn.salah_steps.salah_salawat.title: Send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ
learn.salah_steps.salah_second_rakah.bod: Stand up with Allahu akbar and repeat everything from Al-Fatihah to the second prostration. There is no opening du‘a this time.
learn.salah_steps.salah_second_sujud.bod: Say Allahu akbar and make a second prostration, just like the first.
learn.salah_steps.salah_short_surah.body: In the first two rak'ahs, recite a short surah after Al-Fatihah. Al-Ikhlas is a good one to start with.
learn.salah_steps.salah_short_surah.reci: Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Self-Sufficient on whom all depend. He neither begets nor was He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.
learn.salah_steps.salah_sitting.body: Say Allahu akbar, sit up and be still for a moment.
learn.salah_steps.salah_sitting.recite.m: My Lord, forgive me. My Lord, forgive me.
learn.salah_steps.salah_sitting.title: Sit between the prostrations
learn.salah_steps.salah_sujud.body: Say Allahu akbar and prostrate on forehead and nose, palms, knees and toes, and be still. This is the closest you are to your Lord, so make du‘a here too (Muslim 482).
learn.salah_steps.salah_sujud.recite.mea: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High
learn.salah_steps.salah_sujud.title: Prostrate (sujud)
learn.salah_steps.salah_takbir.body: Raise your hands to your shoulders or ears and say Allahu akbar, then rest your right hand over your left. Where the hands rest differs by school. Hanafi and Hanbali: below the navel (Hanafi women: on the chest); Shafi'i: below the chest, above the navel; many Malikis let the arms hang at the sides. All are valid practice.
learn.salah_steps.salah_takbir.title: Begin with Allahu akbar
learn.salah_steps.salah_tashahhud.body: After the second rak'ah's prostrations, sit and recite the tashahhud.
learn.salah_steps.salah_tashahhud.recite: All greetings, prayers and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.
learn.salah_steps.salah_tashahhud.title: Sit for the tashahhud
learn.salah_steps.salah_taslim.body: Turn your head to the right and say the salam, then turn to the left and say it again. Your prayer is complete, alhamdulillah.
learn.salah_steps.salah_taslim.recite.me: Peace and the mercy of Allah be upon you
learn.salah_steps.salah_taslim.title: End with salam
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_arms.body: Wash your right arm from the fingertips up to and including the elbow, three times, then the left.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_arms.title: Wash your arms
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_bismillah.body: Begin by mentioning the name of Allah.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_bismillah.title: Say Bismillah
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_ears.body: Wipe the inside of your ears with your index fingers and the back with your thumbs, once.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_ears.title: Wipe your ears
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_face.body: Wash your whole face, from the hairline to the chin and from ear to ear, three times.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_face.title: Wash your face
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_feet.body: Wash your right foot up to and including the ankle, three times, getting between the toes, then the left.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_feet.title: Wash your feet
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_hands.body: Wash both hands up to the wrists, three times.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_hands.title: Wash your hands
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_head.body: Wipe your head once with wet hands, from front to back and back to the front again, as the Prophet ﷺ did. How much must be wiped differs by school. Maliki and Hanbali: the whole head; Hanafi: at least a quarter; Shafi'i: any part. Wiping the whole head covers all views.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_head.title: Wipe your head
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_intention.body: Intend in your heart that you are purifying yourself for prayer; there is nothing to say out loud. Most scholars count this intention as required, while Hanafis count it as sunnah.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_intention.title: Intend in your heart
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_mouth_nose.body: Rinse your mouth and sniff water into your nose and blow it out, three times. One handful of water for both is fine.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_mouth_nose.title: Mouth and nose
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_order.body: Do the steps in this order and without long breaks in between. Washing each part once or twice is valid too; three times is the full sunnah, so don't go beyond three.
learn.wudu_steps.wudu_order.title: Keep the order, no long pauses
milestone.fajr_7.meaning: "Whoever prays the two cool prayers (Fajr and 'Asr) will enter Paradise."
milestone.fajr_7.title: Seven Fajr prayers
milestone.first_full_salah_day.meaning: "That is the likeness of the five prayers: through them Allah wipes away sins." (Like bathing in a river at your door five times a day.)
milestone.first_full_salah_day.title: All five prayers in one day
milestone.first_reflection.meaning: "O you who believe, fear Allah, and let every soul look to what it has sent forth for tomorrow. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do."
milestone.first_reflection.title: Your first reflection
milestone.first_step.meaning: Allah says: "If he draws near to Me a hand-span, I draw near to him an arm's length… and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running."
milestone.first_step.title: Your first step
milestone.halfway.meaning: "For indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease."
milestone.halfway.title: Halfway through your journey
milestone.journey_complete.meaning: "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you."
milestone.journey_complete.title: Thirty days complete
milestone.streak_7.meaning: "And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty (death)."
milestone.streak_7.title: Seven days in a row
milestone.tasbih_1000.meaning: "Is any of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds each day? He glorifies Allah a hundred times, and a thousand good deeds are written for him or a thousand sins are removed."
milestone.tasbih_1000.title: A thousand glorifications
milestone.three_days.meaning: "And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good."
milestone.three_days.title: Three days of showing up
milestone.week_one.meaning: "The religion is ease… so do what is right, come as close as you can, and rejoice."
milestone.week_one.title: One week on the path
